title: LOGO
author: Prabhanjan K. Mishra
text:
I dreamt of a flute,
heard a flutist playing somewhere
serenading the still night.

A shred of a melody
haunted the silent air
caressing its wounds.

Radha might have taken it
as her heartthrob`s fickle mischief,
Mira as her Lord`s soothing fingers.

Again my eyes heavy with sleep
saw a lonely lady weeping in a forest, the trees around holding helpless breath.

Unable to lift a finger, their covenant`s
peremptory condition, rooted to the soil,
but they drip dew to soothe her tears.

An old ascetic with a bamboo bow gave
shelter to her helplessness in his hut,
his bow holding predators at bay.

I woke into a nostalgic morning.
Pains of Radha, Mira, and Sita
haunted my guilt like scalding embers.

Radha`s lonely tears were turning
into hot and humid summer breath.
Her rage salvaging her yearning youth.

Mira collected her memory and folded
them back to her heart to carry them
to her grave that she waited with joy.

Sita felt betrayed but her husband
was a king. In his scale, she was pitted against thousands of his subjects.

Even love has been a tender politics,
its logo taking chimeral nuances, and
tongues from the strange rubric of time.
